text:
Quinton Byfield is the Kings' best example of a player doing more than his numbers say. He has eight points in 19 games, below last season's pace, but his own chances are up to 1.23 expected goals per 60 minutes from 0.82 (expected goals measure the quality of chances), he is on the ice for 81% of the team's power-play chances, and Los Angeles takes 55% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, nearly seven points better than without him.

The problem is the finish around him. The Kings have scored about 9.9 fewer goals than their chances with him on the ice, and that usually swings back. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 90th percentile for driving play last season. The second overall pick of 2020, one spot ahead of Tim Stützle, is one point from 200 for his career. Our range has him around 26 goals. If his linemates start finishing, the breakout people expected will show up on the scoresheet too.
